body:
Related: vim/vim#20231
Closes #39819

## Problem

This follows the recent `fnamemodify(..., ':h')` root handling work, but Windows UNC paths have a separate root rule: the server/share pair is the root.

`fnamemodify(..., ':h')` can treat the share name as an ordinary path component and strip `//foo/C$` back to `//foo`.

## Solution

Preserve basic Windows UNC share roots when computing the head.

comment_data.body: would appreciate review on the c aspect especially; tried to prioritize simplicity over conciseness in the impl
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -52,6 +52,61 @@
 
 static const char e_error_while_writing_str[] = N_("E80: Error while writing: %s");
 
+#ifdef MSWIN
+// Windows UNC paths are rooted at the server/share pair:
+//   //server/share/path => //server/share
+// This covers ordinary shares, including administrative shares like C$.
+// Device paths (//?/..., //./...) use different prefix rules.
+// https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/io/file-path-formats#unc-paths
+static bool path_is_basic_unc_share_root(char *fname, size_t fnamelen, char **sharep, char **rootp)

comment_data.body:
Assuming we split a path into the three parts below (pending better names and structure), we could extend `os_fileinfo2()` to expose the offset of `rest` (`rest_off`), allowing us to replace `get_path_head()` here. :)
```shell
# windows dos path
C:/foo/bar
^  ^------- rest
+---------- root

# windows device path
////?/C:/foo/bar
  ^   ^  ^------- rest
  |   +---------- root
  +-------------- prefix

# windows unc path
////server/share/foo/bar
  ^ ^            ^------- rest
  | +-------------------- root
  +---------------------- prefix

# windows device unc path
////?/UNC/server/share/foo/bar
  ^       ^            ^------- rest
  |       +-------------------- root
  +---------------------------- prefix
   
# unix path
///foo/bar
  ^^------- rest
  +-------- root
```
Do you want to take this PR over with this refactor then, it's fine w me
